name: Green and red cups coincide
summary: A phase-free Z-spider with two outputs equals a phase-free X-spider with two outputs: both are the cup.
description:
Each colour of spider induces a compact structure: a phase-free spider with two outputs is a 'cup' (the Bell state $|00\rangle+|11\rangle$), and one with two inputs is a 'cap'. This rule says that the compact structures of the Z- and the X-spiders are the same: indeed $|00\rangle + |11\rangle = |{+}{+}\rangle + |{-}{-}\rangle$.

In the simplified stabilizer ZX-calculus of Backens, Perdrix and Wang this is the second half of the axiom (S3′), called (S3′R) in their follow-up paper; the first half, (S3′L), says that the green cup is the cup of the ambient category, i.e. [identity removal](../identity-removal/) with the wire bent. Backens, Perdrix and Wang could not decide whether (S3′R) is necessary; Stoltz later showed that it cannot be derived from the other rules.

In the usual presentation, where 'only connectivity matters', this rule follows from identity removal for both colours.
